title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier plus a bounded automated‑repair budget increases the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. Each paired intent produced one shared_initial candidate reused for both conditions: baseline (accept single candidate) and guarded (validator + ≤1 automated repair). Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the chosen synthetic suite and a single‑repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We release a complete preregistration, execution, and analysis bundle and interpret results with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational policies.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to NetOps tasks including intent→configuration translation, configuration synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment network changes, semantic correctness properties (sequencing constraints, reachability, policy preservation) are operationally critical and are not assured by superficial syntactic checks. A prevalent engineering pattern is generate→validate→repair: pair a generative model with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair to reduce operational risk. Yet measurable benefit from guarded pipelines depends on (i) the experimental estimand (what is held fixed), (ii) single‑shot generator quality, (iii) validator expressiveness, and (iv) permitted repair budget.

We preregistered a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) to quantify the deterministic rescue achievable when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. For each intent the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate using gpt-5-mini and compared: baseline — accept the single candidate; guarded — run a deterministic validator and allow at most one automated repair, which is re‑validated deterministically. The primary research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair?

Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under a shared_initial estimand that conditions on a single LLM draw per intent; (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle including validator traces and the single automated repair transcript archived with the run; and (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation of estimator conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and system papers document rapid progress in LLM‑assisted NetOps and emphasize tool‑augmented architectures, generate→validate→repair scaffolds, and hybrid repair approaches. Prior work demonstrates improvements from adding deterministic checks, but reported magnitudes vary with validator coverage and task distributions [1–4]. Planner‑centric and ReAct‑style frameworks let LLMs call external validators or simulators to decompose workflows, enabling richer coordination but conflating benefits from validation with benefits from resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration [5]. Literature on hallucination detection and deterministic safety nets emphasizes detection and mitigation techniques (entropy‑based detectors, retrieval augmentation, self‑reflection) that reduce false positives but remain sensitive to validator semantics and domain threat models [6].

Two methodological themes motivated our design: (a) many prior evaluations mix deterministic‑validation benefits with resampling or iterative generation, making the isolated contribution of post‑generation checking difficult to bound; and (b) publicly available NetOps benchmarks have often emphasized syntactic/template correctness rather than semantically rich invariants (reachability, sequencing, policy preservation), limiting operational generality. Our study explicitly conditions on a single LLM draw and a bounded repair budget to isolate the deterministic rescue that constrained post‑hoc checking and limited automated editing can deliver.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We froze the confirmatory design before observing main results under study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001. The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) on N = 300 paired intents after applying preregistered inclusion/exclusion rules. The confirmatory analysis uses an exact McNemar two‑sided test and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). The preregistration specified a pilot for discordance estimation; the pilot was not executed prior to the main run.

Task generation and stratification. The synthetic_topology_suite was generated deterministically and stratified into three difficulty strata (low/medium/high) using manifest metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count). The confirmatory sample drew 100 pairs per stratum. Each task manifest encodes natural‑language intent, initial/expected final device states, sequencing invariants (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), preservation constraints, and protected interfaces.

Shared_initial protocol and model configuration. To measure deterministic rescue alone we implemented a shared_initial estimand: produce exactly one shared_initial candidate per pair (requested_model = gpt-5-mini) and reuse it for both conditions. This prevents differences due to resampling and isolates validator + bounded repair effects. The run enforced model_call budget constraints (maximum_model_calls as preregistered) and limited repair attempts to ≤1 per pair.

Validator and repair operator. Semantic evaluation used a deterministic validator implementing the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule. The validator deterministically checks sequencing invariants, required command counts, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability invariants encoded in the suite, and forbidden‑template protections. Scoring is binary (unflagged == pass). The guarded pipeline permits at most one constrained automated repair: a localized edit operator limited to inserting or reordering sequencing commands (e.g., inserting an explicit 'admin down' prior to VLAN/MTU changes). Repairs are applied only when the validator flags the shared_initial candidate and are re‑validated deterministically; repaired candidates that remain flagged count as failures for guarded in the primary analysis.

Contamination controls and exclusions. The preregistration included deterministic contamination checks (negative controls and invariant comparisons). A pair is excluded from confirmatory analysis only if both pipeline calls fail due to provider/infrastructure outages; single‑call failures are handled per the preregistered complete_pair_primary rule and subjected to sensitivity analysis. Execution recorded no dual‑call outages and no exclusions for the confirmatory sample.

Execution auditing and reproducibility. The run used an adapter enforcing the preregistered protocol and archived complete execution and analysis artifacts. Instrumentation recorded planned_episode_count = 600, completed_episode_count = 600 (complete_pair_count = 300), and model_calls_used = 301. Provider audit logs indicated one repair stage was invoked across the run; deterministic reconciliation confirmed accounting consistency. All design, execution, validator traces, repair transcripts, and analysis inputs are archived in the run bundle to permit deterministic replay of the confirmatory executor.
sections.results:
Execution integrity. The adapter completed the confirmatory run with completed_episode_count = 600 and complete_pair_count = 300 under the shared_initial protocol. Provider audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 301 (300 shared_initial generations plus one repair invocation) and stage_counts consistent with the preregistered constraints. Deterministic reconciliation reported consistent episode accounting and no excluded pairs.

Primary outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667; guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The exact two‑sided McNemar test operating on discordant counts returned p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01]. With total discordance m = 1 the exact test has limited sensitivity; the bootstrap CI bounds plausible absolute improvement under this estimand and suite to at most one percentage point.

Stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Per‑stratum tallies were: low baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100 and guarded = 100/100. The single discordant pair occurred in the high stratum. The permitted automated repair was invoked for that episode: the validator initially flagged a sequencing omission (required 'admin down' missing before VLAN/MTU change); the constrained repair inserted the missing sequencing step and the validator then reported a deterministic pass. The repair therefore produced one deterministic rescue under the allowed repair budget. Repair and validator before/after traces are archived; the manuscript reports the semantic diagnostic summary rather than verbatim provider transcripts.
sections.discussion:
Estimand conditioning and operational interpretation. The shared_initial estimand models operational policies that restrict model calls per change request (cost, latency, governance). Under such policies the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to an identical candidate. Workflows that permit resampling, verifier‑guided regeneration, or interactive steering address a different estimand and commonly achieve higher success by exploiting generator variance; evaluations for those workflows should be preregistered accordingly.

Ceiling effects and pilot omission. The preregistration targeted detecting a 10 percentage‑point absolute improvement with planned power ≈0.8 based on a pilot to estimate discordance. Because the optional pilot was not executed, the main run confronted a near‑ceiling baseline (299/300), yielding minimal discordance (m = 1) and reduced sensitivity to small absolute differences. This outcome reinforces the practical value of brief calibration pilots when generator performance may approach ceiling on a chosen suite.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The single observed failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, forbidden ACL removal) were not observed at scale in this synthetic suite. The guarded pipeline's marginal utility depends on (a) the deployment distribution of failure modes and (b) validator expressiveness. Richer validators detecting additional semantic properties would likely alter observed rescue rates; conversely, operator policies that forbid automated edits limit guarded pipelines to detection and escalation.

Repair budget tradeoffs. We intentionally limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to quantify bounded deterministic rescue. Iterative repair, larger edit operators, or verifier‑guided generation would increase rescue opportunities but measure a different operational quantity. Our empirical repair_stage_count = 1 (one repair across 300 pairs) shows that bounded repair can produce deterministic rescue with negligible extra model‑call cost in scenarios similar to our suite.

Implications for NetOps CI/CD. Organizations must align evaluation estimands with operational policies: if pipelines allow multiple model calls, evaluations should permit resampling and interactive steering. If model calls are tightly budgeted, the shared_initial estimand provides a meaningful operational bound on deterministic verifier/repair rescue per single candidate. Archived artifacts (design, validator traces, repair transcript, and accounting logs) enable practitioners to inspect whether bounded automated edits would meet local governance requirements.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). Deterministic validator+repair rescued one sequencing omission under the bounded repair budget. The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity to small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. We release full preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts so follow‑up studies can vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distribution, or repair budget to evaluate alternative operational regimes.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated deterministically; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase validator marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and the declared deterministic validator were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.
Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced sensitivity to small absolute improvements.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run prior to the main confirmatory run.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from permitting independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one constrained automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
